text:
diana: Quick sync — updating runtime performance metric defs for the new dashboard. Proposals:
- Split TTFT into cold_start_ttft (first token after model load) and steady_ttft (after warm-up).
- Compute p95 over warm requests only.
- Add tok/s_warm (tokens/sec from completed warm requests).
Need opinions + a quick :thumbsup: from runtime owners.

mike: +1 to splitting TTFT. How are we detecting "warm"? KV cache hit seems noisy on some models.

jess: Suggest warm = (kv_cache_hit == 1) OR (session_request_index > 1). For dashboards use a warm label and show cold_start p50/p95 separately so first-token regressions are visible.

rahul: I'll open a PR with PromQL and new grafana panels. Quick PromQL drafts I used for sanity:
```
# steady TTFT p95 (warm)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ttft_seconds_bucket{warm="true"}[5m])) by (le))

# tok/s warm — requests/sec * avg tokens per request (1m window)
sum(rate(completed_requests_total{warm="true"}[1m])) * avg_over_time(avg_tokens_per_request{warm="true"}[1m])
```
I'll refine and link the PR: github.com/redwood/runtime-metrics/pull/42

ci-bot: PR opened: runtime-metrics#42 by rahul — "dashboard: warm/cold ttft + toks/s_warm" (checks: unit tests pending)

diana: Two asks before merge:
1) Add sampling windows to panel descriptions (5m rolling for latency, 1m for throughput).
2) Emit baseline tags so alerts can compare to a 7d baseline.
Also propose alert threshold: fire when p95_warm increases > 15% vs 7d baseline for 30m.

mike: pinging @eng-infra for cost impact of extra scrape labels/cardinality. :wave:

jess: I'll review the PR today. If all good we can push dashboards to staging by EOD.
